audit.why: Akshan owns levels 1-3 on range and the three-hit passive shield; the lane flips to Sejuani at 6 and stays there. The entry already says this and the packet's levelChart agrees. Heroic Swing at 18s rank 1 against Arctic Assault at 18s rank 1 is why levels 2-3 are a standoff rather than a loss — neither side can commit without spending their only mobility.

Level 6, first tank item and two items are the right three spikes and the entry lists them in the right order. Level 6 is the real flip and spikes[1] correctly puts it there; what was missing was the reason, which I added rather than moving the spike.
audit.corrected: spikes[1].text now states what changes at 6 (the reveal), not just that something does.

audit.whatIsWrong: The interaction that decides this matchup is absent from all seventeen fields: Glacial Prison reveals stealth, and Going Rogue is Akshan's entire pattern. The entry also never mentions that Heroic Swing breaks on champion collision.
audit.why: Riot's Glacial Prison text carries a stealth reveal and Sejuani's kit flags it as her answer to stealth champions. Akshan's Going Rogue puts him in camouflage on a cooldown that falls from 18s at rank 1 to 2 seconds at rank 5 — by late game it is permanently available, and it is the reason he is impossible to catch. Sejuani's ultimate is the single ability in her kit that undoes it, and the entry instead sells R as 'a long-range comet' for catching him mid-swing. Second: Heroic Swing's own text says he 'gets knocked off when colliding with champions or terrain', which means walking into the arc, or charging it with Arctic Assault, ends the swing outright. Both of these convert R and Q from generic tools into specific answers to his two escape buttons.
audit.corrected: The reveal is now stated in spikes[1].text, whys[4], report[5].t, breakdown.cooldowns and late, with Going Rogue's 18s-to-2s cooldown range. The Heroic Swing collision break is stated in wants.you[2] and report[5].t.

audit.whatIsWrong: late says 'his revive passive punishes single-targeting, so target him last'.
audit.why: Dirty Fighting does not resurrect anything. The revive is on Going Rogue: Akshan marks enemies as Scoundrels when they kill his allies, and resurrects those allies if he kills the Scoundrel. It is triggered by him getting a kill, not by your team focusing him — so 'target him last' is backwards. If anything he should be killed early, before he can cash a Scoundrel mark. I removed the claim rather than replace it with the inverse instruction, since whether to prioritise him depends on whether marks are live.
audit.corrected: late no longer contains the revive claim; the space now carries the Going Rogue reveal, which is the actionable point at that stage.
sources: champ-data/_kits/akshan.json (W Going Rogue description; P Dirty Fighting description)

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns names Heroic Swing as 'matchup-defining' with no number and does not mention Going Rogue at all.
audit.why: Both of his relevant cooldowns are missing, and the one that matters most changes by a factor of nine across ranks. Telling a reader to 'fight while it is down' without saying 18 seconds, and never telling them that his escape becomes a 2-second cooldown, means they will plan a late-game catch that cannot work without R.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns now gives 18s for Heroic Swing and the 18s-to-2s range for Going Rogue, and names R as the only reveal.

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.foe[2] says his poke means 'your passive armor bonus never fully charges'.
audit.why: Frost Armor does not charge. Riot's text: it is gained after being out of combat and persists briefly after Sejuani takes damage. Chip poke does not slow a meter — it keeps her in combat so the armour never returns. That is a different instruction for the reader: break contact, do not merely avoid the last hundred damage.
audit.corrected: wants.foe[2] now describes keeping her in combat so Frost Armor never comes back.

notes:
spikes[1].text described Glacial Prison as a 'long-range comet'. Comet is a rune, not part of Sejuani's kit, and a reader scanning for it in her ability list will not find it. Replaced with the bola's actual 1300 range.

The _missing-interactions entry for sejuani/akshan says 'you have no dash'. Arctic Assault is a 650-range charge, so that premise is wrong; I used the reveal from the same entry, which is correct, and ignored the no-dash framing. If that rule is generating advice elsewhere in the champion it will be telling Sejuani players they have no mobility.

UNVERIFIED, left alone: whether Glacial Prison's bola can collide with a champion who is camouflaged but not yet revealed, i.e. whether the reveal happens on hit or whether he must be visible first. Riot's text does not say, so late and spikes[1] are written so the advice holds either way.
